The main takeaway from our work is that

the high-temperature series of the standard three-dimensional Ising Hamiltonian can be used to obtain accurate results for the critical equation of states of improved models, provided that the leading scaling corrections are properly taken into account.

, by using a suitable parametrization of the equation of state, it is possible to extract the universal critical exponents and the leading scaling correction exponent Delta from high-temperature expansion series, even when the latter are truncated at a relatively low order.
the 25th order is sufficient to extract critical parameters with a precision comparable to that obtained from high-temperature expansion studies at the 30th order.
